intent: fetch command: init container looks up, verifies and writes the archive, always fail-open

title: fetch exits 0 on every caught problem; --strict opts into failing
why: An init container that exits non-zero blocks the pod, so even misconfiguration must degrade to an uncached start with a logged reason.
alternative: Exit 2 on usage or config errors — rejected: surfaces mistakes immediately but can block startup

title: clear stale flags and manifest before every fetch; write new ones atomically
why: A miss must not leave flags from a previous run pointing at an old archive; temp-file-then-move keeps readers from seeing a half-written flags file.
alternative: Overwrite only on hit — rejected: stale flags survive a miss

title: try AOT then AppCDS, one fingerprint per cache type, and recheck the stored manifest against the live one
why: The cache type is part of the fingerprint, so each type is its own lookup; the manifest recheck guards against a store entry that does not describe this environment.
alternative: Single lookup by one cache type — rejected: loses the AOT to AppCDS fallback chain in the plan

name: ArchiveFetcher
role: Looks candidates up in order, verifies, writes archive, manifest and flags; returns HIT or MISS with notes and never throws for store problems
conditions: Clears stale flags first; flags file is one line with the runtime JVM flag

name: fetch command
role: Init-container entry point; computes live manifests from --jar, JDK and options like build does
conditions: Must run where the app JAR and JDK are present (app image); exit 0 unless --strict

subject: JAR modification times
why: The JVM checks classpath JAR mtimes but the fingerprint ignores them, so an archive can be fetched yet silently ignored by the JVM if files were re-extracted later (PLAN open decision 6, handled with run)

subject: Same options as training
why: fetch must receive the same --jvm-arg, --image-digest and work-dir layout as build, or the live fingerprint differs and nothing is found

intent: Address review: repeatable extraction, parse errors, flags last, stale flags

title: extract into a fresh scratch directory per fetch and delete it afterwards
why: JarExtractor refuses a non-empty destination, so reusing work-dir/app made a second fetch fail after an init container restart. The fingerprint uses entry names and content, never the path, so a throwaway directory is equivalent.
alternative: Reuse a verified earlier extraction — rejected: more state to validate for no fingerprint benefit

title: handle picocli parse and unexpected errors for fetch inside the command, withdrawing stale flags
why: Picocli rejects bad options before call() runs, so the fail-open contract needs parameter and execution exception handlers scoped to the fetch command; other commands keep the default exit 2.
alternative: Document that wrappers must validate arguments — rejected: pushes the pod-blocking risk onto every deployment

title: write the flags file last and withdraw it on any later failure; empty stale flags if they cannot be deleted
why: The flags file is the only thing the launch reads, so it is the commit point. An empty flags file means run plain, so emptying is the fallback when deletion is denied; if neither works the failure is reported and the consumer's manifest check plus the JVM's refusal of mismatched archives remain the guard.
alternative: Exit non-zero when stale flags cannot be removed — rejected: blocks the pod, against §3, while the JVM already ignores mismatched archives (§1)

subject: picocli parse errors bypass call()
why: Parameter exceptions are handled by the top-level CommandLine's handler before the command runs, so command-specific fail-open needs a handler that checks the failing subcommand

subject: Read-only directory tests
why: They rely on a non-root user; the tests skip themselves when the directory is still writable
